method: Floor = the lowest documented value of every component that is outside the core by definition, plus the core's lowest published bound. Ceiling = the highest documented value of each, assuming the fishing figure sits entirely outside the core. Beyond the ceiling the toll is unknown, not zero.

layers.label: Core: unintentional drowning
layers.note: Two models of the same year. The spread is the uncertainty, not new deaths.

layers.label: Fishing work (share outside the core unknown)
layers.note: 24,000 to 100,000+ a year across sources and decades. Nobody has published how much is already inside WHO's figure, so the floor is 0 and the ceiling assumes none of it is.

layers.label: Flood and disaster drownings
layers.note: 75% of flood-disaster deaths (WHO) applied to EM-DAT yearly totals, which swing several-fold.

layers.label: Migrants at sea
layers.note: Recorded deaths are a minimum; IOM estimates about 1,500 more in wrecks no one recorded.

layers.label: Ferry accidents
layers.note: An old estimate from the Worldwide Ferry Safety Association, which said the true figure could be double.

layers.label: Intentional and undetermined intent
layers.note: A different problem with different prevention; no primary global figure reproduced here.

nonfatal.label: Non-fatal drownings
nonfatal.note: For every death, four to five people survive a drowning, many with lasting injury. Never added to deaths.
